info.name: RAG FAST API
info.description:
All endpoints for the RAG / Transaction-Log FastAPI backend.

Folders:
- Health
- Documents - Ingestion (upload + job status)
- Documents - Search (hybrid vector + keyword search, variations)
- Logs - Ingestion (push a log file -> Stage 1 parse+insert)
- Logs - Query (job status + line-level entry queries, all filter variations)

Collection variables:
- baseUrl        : server origin (default http://localhost:8000)
- documentJobId  : auto-set by 'Upload document' test script
- logJobId       : auto-set by 'Ingest log file' test script
- logFilePath    : default file for log ingest (points at the real mnp-logs sample)
- docFilePath    : default file for document upload (set your own)

Tip: run 'Ingest log file' (or 'Upload document') first; its test script stores the returned job_id into the collection variable, so the matching 'Get ... job' request just works.

MULTI-TENANT: every /logs/* request must send the header `X-Customer-Code: {{customerCode}}` (default tenant `mnp`). Document/Search/Health endpoints are NOT tenant-scoped and need no header.

request.description: Create-or-attach. If customer_code is new -> creates the tenant (201). If customer_code already exists -> attaches display_name as an additional username under that tenant (200, idempotent; the code is never duplicated). 400 on a malformed code. Fetch a single tenant by code. Response now also includes a display_names[] array of every username attached to this tenant.
List every display name (username) attached to this tenant. 404 if the customer_code is unknown.

Attach an additional display name (username) to an existing tenant. 201 returns the new row; 404 if the code is unknown; 409 if the same name is already attached. Test script stores the new id into displayNameId for the delete request below.
Detach a display name from a tenant by its id (204 on success). 404 if the tenant or the id is unknown. Uses the displayNameId set by 'Add display name'.
Retire a tenant from ingestion + selection (active=false) without deleting its data. Set active:true to re-enable.

request.description: Run Stage 2 over ALL of this customer's entries. Default = full rebuild (historical backfill / repair); ?incremental=true = unsealed live tail only. For a normal upload session prefer 'Finalize regroup', which regroups only the windows you just touched (scoped + lossless) instead of the whole table.

request.description: Cheap check (NOT guarded): does this customer have log windows pending regroup? Returns { pending, pending_windows, oldest_pending_at }. Transaction reads do NOT block on this — they return last-good data plus the same flag (soft gate). pending=true means the newest ingested tail isn't stitched in yet; POST /logs/regroup/finalize (or read with finalize=true) to include it.

header.description: Tenant/customer this request operates on (required on all /logs endpoints).

request.description: Confirm 'I'm done uploading this session' -> regroups ONLY the time windows your recent uploads touched (scoped + padded; lossless), then clears them as pending. NON-BLOCKING: returns 202 with { run_id, status:'running', poll } and runs in the background, so a long/sparse batch can't time out the request. The test script saves run_id -> regroupRunId; poll 'Get regroup run status' until status is completed (or failed). Idempotent: a run with nothing pending completes with windows:0. Call once after the last file of a session.

request.description: Poll the async finalize started by 'Finalize regroup'. Returns { status, windows, pending_consumed, error, result, created_at, finished_at }. status is `running` until the background regroup finishes, then `completed` (with stats) or `failed` (with error; the pending windows stay open so you can retry). Uses regroupRunId captured by the finalize test script.

item.name: Logs - Remote SSH Sources
item.description: Pull M3 logs from one or more Windows Servers (OpenSSH) over SFTP. Configure a source, test the connection (pins the host fingerprint), then trigger an async fetch and poll the run. Run order: Create -> Test -> Fetch -> Get run. Secrets (private_key/key_passphrase) are write-only; GET never returns them.

Stores sshSourceId for the next requests.
